paragraphs.text: 1. COME to this sacrifice of ours, O Agni, threefold, with seven threads and five divisions.
paragraphs.original: इमं नो अग्न उप यज्ञमेहि पञ्चयामं त्रिवृतं सप्ततन्तुम् ।
paragraphs.translit: imaṃ no agna upa yajñamehi pañcayāmaṃ trivṛtaṃ saptatantum |

paragraphs.text: Be our oblation-bearer and preceder: thou hast lain long enough in during darkness.
paragraphs.original: असो हव्यवाळुत नः पुरोगा ज्योगेव दीर्घं तम आशयिष्ठाः
paragraphs.translit: aso havyavāḷuta naḥ purogā jyogeva dīrghaṃ tama āśayiṣṭhāḥ

paragraphs.text: 2. I come a God foreseeing from the godless to immortality by secret pathways,
While I, ungracious one, desert the gracious, leave mine own friends and seek the kin of strangers.
3. I, looking to the guest of other lineage, have founded many a rule of Law and Order.
paragraphs.original: पश्यन्नन्यस्या अतिथिं वयाया ऋतस्य धाम वि मिमे पुरूणि ।
paragraphs.translit: paśyannanyasyā atithiṃ vayāyā ṛtasya dhāma vi mime purūṇi |

paragraphs.text: I bid farewell to the Great God, the Father, and, for neglect, obtain my share of worship.
4. I tarried many a year within this altar: I leave the Father, for my choice is Indra.
paragraphs.original: बह्वीः समा अकरमन्तरस्मिन्निन्द्रं वृणानः पितरं जहामि ।
paragraphs.translit: bahvīḥ samā akaramantarasminnindraṃ vṛṇānaḥ pitaraṃ jahāmi |

paragraphs.text: Away pass Agni, Varuna and Soma. Rule ever changes: this I come to favour.
paragraphs.original: अग्निः सोमो वरुणस्ते च्यवन्ते पर्यावर्द्राष्ट्रं तदवाम्यायन्
paragraphs.translit: agniḥ somo varuṇaste cyavante paryāvardrāṣṭraṃ tadavāmyāyan

paragraphs.text: 5. These Asuras have lost their powers of magic. But thou, O Varuna, if thou dost love me,
paragraphs.original: निर्माया उ त्ये असुरा अभूवन्त्वं च मा वरुण कामयासे ।
paragraphs.translit: nirmāyā u tye asurā abhūvantvaṃ ca mā varuṇa kāmayāse |

paragraphs.text: O King, discerning truth and right from falsehood, come and be Lord and Ruler of my kingdom.
6. Here is the light of heaven, here all is lovely; here there is radiance, here is air's wide region.
Let us two slaughter Vrtra. Forth, O Soma! Thou art oblation: we therewith will serve thee.
paragraphs.original: हनाव वृत्रं निरेहि सोम हविष्ट्वा सन्तं हविषा यजाम
paragraphs.translit: hanāva vṛtraṃ nirehi soma haviṣṭvā santaṃ haviṣā yajāma

paragraphs.text: 7. The Sage hath fixed his form by wisdom in the heavens: Varuna with no violence let the waters flow.
paragraphs.original: कविः कवित्वा दिवि रूपमासजदप्रभूती वरुणो निरपः सृजत् ।
paragraphs.translit: kaviḥ kavitvā divi rūpamāsajadaprabhūtī varuṇo nirapaḥ sṛjat |

paragraphs.text: Like women-folk, the floods that bring prosperity have you lit his hue and colour as they gleamed and shone.
paragraphs.original: क्षेमं कृण्वाना जनयो न सिन्धवस्ता अस्य वर्णं शुचयो भरिभ्रति
paragraphs.translit: kṣemaṃ kṛṇvānā janayo na sindhavastā asya varṇaṃ śucayo bharibhrati

paragraphs.text: 8. These wait upon his loftiest power and vigour: he dwells in these who triumph in their Godhead;
paragraphs.original: ता अस्य ज्येष्ठमिन्द्रियं सचन्ते ता ईमा क्षेति स्वधया मदन्तीः ।
paragraphs.translit: tā asya jyeṣṭhamindriyaṃ sacante tā īmā kṣeti svadhayā madantīḥ |

paragraphs.text: And they, like people who elect their ruler, have in abhorrence turned away from Vrtra.
paragraphs.original: ता ईं विशो न राजानं वृणाना बीभत्सुवो अप वृत्रादतिष्ठन्
paragraphs.translit: tā īṃ viśo na rājānaṃ vṛṇānā bībhatsuvo apa vṛtrādatiṣṭhan

paragraphs.text: 9. They call him Swan, the abhorrent floods' Companion, moving in friendship with celestial Waters.
paragraphs.original: बीभत्सूनां सयुजं हंसमाहुरपां दिव्यानां सख्ये चरन्तम् ।
paragraphs.translit: bībhatsūnāṃ sayujaṃ haṃsamāhurapāṃ divyānāṃ sakhye carantam |

paragraphs.text: The poets in their thought have looked on Indra swiftly approaching when Anustup calls him.
paragraphs.original: अनुष्टुभमनु चर्चूर्यमाणमिन्द्रं नि चिक्युः कवयो मनीषा
paragraphs.translit: anuṣṭubhamanu carcūryamāṇamindraṃ ni cikyuḥ kavayo manīṣā
